made.note: Batch 41 is bigger than last week: 94 files, nine concepts, 29 adsets, in three upload days. Wednesday for Latina, Local Dating English and Mature; Thursday for International Friend; Friday for Gringo, Passport Bro and the rest. So some adsets have five days of data, some only three.

scoreboard.title:
Last week refresh status:
4 worked, 8 almost, 1 watch, 6 worse, 9 missed
scoreboard.foot: Verdicts as on the rules slide. Early reads: final call at week 4 (week of 30 Nov). Next: one slide per refresh, biggest priority first, then its action items.
scoreboard.note: Nothing is final after three to five days. Four worked, eight almost, one to watch, six got worse and nine missed. We go in priority order, spend times how bad the read is: Passport Bro first, then Local Dating, International Friend, Latina, Gringo, Mature.

personas.title: Passport Bro Refresh: Dreamlife
personas.sub: Result: 1 almost, 1 missed · dreamlife is #3 on iOS with 15%
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days: an early read) · rows: in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
personas.note: Dreamlife, the Gringo winner, went into Passport Bro on Friday. After three days it is third on iOS with 15 percent and ROAS went up to 0.37, still under the bar. On Android it got 6 percent and the adset slipped under 0.40.

actions.title: Passport Bro: the October winners are wearing out; bring back wanted

rows.action: J2 · wanted’s “how life feels after marrying her”, new couple and kitchen. #1 here for 11 weeks, the longest reign.
Week 2: #3 on iOS, ROAS 0.31 → 0.37.
0.45 → 0.40: datingcontest (0.53 → 0.35) and boysvmen (0.48 → 0.41) faded. Combo is fine (0.44). Budget flat: hold.

actions.foot: Android, week of 26 Oct vs 2 Nov: budget $769/day both weeks, no ads switched off. Priority numbers run across the deck.
actions.note: Android didn't drop because of combo: combo is the best of the big ads at 0.44. It dropped because the two October winners, datingcontest and boysvmen, are wearing out. So the next batch brings back wanted, Passport Bro's longest-running winner, in a new couple and kitchen.

personas.title: Local Dating: Colosseum (EN), Talkinghead (ES)
personas.sub: Result: 1 worked, 1 almost, 2 got worse, 1 missed · colosseum lifts iOS EN, sinks Android EN
personas.foot: Before = 7 days before upload · After = upload – 8 Nov (EN from Wed 4 Nov, 5 days; ES from Fri 6 Nov, 3 days) · Android ES is a new adset (6 Nov)
personas.note: Colosseum 50/50 is the new concept from Teddy and Kim. On iOS it is second with 43 percent and the adset went up to 0.52. On both Android adsets it took 28 to 41 percent and ROAS dropped to 0.30 and 0.22. Same ads, opposite results by OS. Spanish got talkinghead variants, too small to count yet.

actions.title: Copy colosseum into Spanish, pull it from Android, find out why it splits

rows.action: Both EN winners say dating apps are a fight men lose (datingcontest’s contest skit; colosseum’s 80 men vs 20 women). Brief the successor on that message with a new visual, both OS.
Why does colosseum lift iOS and sink Android? Compare countries, hook rate and who installs before the next EN brief.
J1: make a Spanish colosseum. It worked on iOS EN (🥈 43%, 0.44 → 0.52). Datingcontest made the same EN → ES move and became #1 in both ES adsets.
Pause the colosseum ads in both Android adsets: 28–41% of spend while ROAS fell.
Loc. Dating EN · iOS: keep colosseum on (0.52). Android ES is a 3-day-old adset at 0.21: give it the week.

actions.foot: Read on 3–5 days (4–8 Nov). Messages read from the ad names: to confirm with screenshots. Priority numbers run across the deck.
actions.note: Colosseum is a real winner on iPhone English, so we copy it into Spanish, the same move that made datingcontest number one there. On Android it hurts, so the media buyer pulls it while we find out why.

personas.title: International Friend Refresh: Lipsync
personas.sub: Result: 3 missed · lipsync got under 1% in English
personas.foot: Before = 29 Oct – 4 Nov · After = 5–8 Nov (4 days) · 2 more lipsync files went to Friends ES under a Batch 45 label ($42): not counted
personas.note: Lipsync is new for International Friend, live since Thursday in English and Chinese. It barely got spend: under 1 percent in English, 6 percent in Chinese. Android English is still the problem at 0.31. iOS English is fine at 0.48 on banner.

actions.title: Friends: tweetoverlay’s message still leads after 12 weeks; give it a new visual

rows.action: Same message, new visual: tweetoverlay has led Android EN and ES for 12 weeks (a tweet over a collage of friends from other countries: “Brazil, Italy, Korea friends”). Lipsync got under 1%.
Tweetoverlay worked in CH as a WeChat Moments post; banner leads now. Why do Chinese speakers want foreign friends? Read reviews and comments.
J2: tweetoverlay led PT for 4 weeks before it faded. Bring it back in Portuguese with a new visual, then switch PT back on.
Last week’s pause isn’t done: the internationalfriends ads still spent $380. Pause them.
Friends EN · iOS: banner (car window) has led 16 weeks at 0.48.

actions.foot: Read on 4 days (5–8 Nov). Ad-name read of tweetoverlay: to confirm with screenshots. Priority numbers run across the deck.
actions.note: Tweetoverlay has led International Friend for twelve weeks, so its message works; the visual is what's tired. The next English brief keeps the message and changes the visual. Portuguese gets tweetoverlay back. Chinese still needs its research.

personas.title: Latina Lover Refresh: Dancing + Sliders
personas.sub: Result: 2 almost, 2 got worse, 1 missed · dancing took #1 in EN, ROAS stays under 0.32
personas.foot: Before = 28 Oct – 3 Nov · After = 4–8 Nov (5 days) · share = dancing + sliders
personas.note: Dancing variants and the new sliders went live on Wednesday. Dancing took #1 in both English adsets within five days, about three quarters of spend, but ROAS stayed low: 0.31 on Android, 0.27 on iOS. In Portuguese it took 46 percent and ROAS fell. Spanish iOS is healthy on banner.

actions.title: Dancing hooks viewers, not buyers: keep the dance, change the message

rows.action: New angle · keep dancing’s opening (best hook rate, 0.33), say wanted’s “in a mood to talk”: 20 buyers per 100 installs vs dancing’s 6–9.
J2 · banner, #1 here for 14 weeks, with a new photo.
New angle · the Latina EN set, in Spanish.
Pause dancing: 75% of spend at 0.28; its installers buy half as often as banner’s (6 vs 12 per 100).
Pause dancing: 46% of spend while ROAS fell 0.27 → 0.23.

actions.foot: Not the countries: on Android the country mix helped (+0.02); ROAS fell inside the same countries (−0.03). Latina EN Android and PT iOS are at 3 strikes.
actions.note: Meta pushes dancing because people stop and watch it: it has the best hook rate in the adset. But the people it brings in don't pay: half as many buyers per install as banner or wanted. It isn't a country shift; the same countries got worse. So we keep the dance as the opening and change what it says to wanted's message, the one that brings payers. Two adsets are at three strikes, so the media buyer pauses dancing there now.

personas.title: Gringo Lover Refresh: Flirted Too Hard + Lipsync
personas.sub: Result: 2 worked, 2 almost, 1 watch, 1 got worse, 3 missed · dreamlife took #1 in TH
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days: an early read) · rows: in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
personas.note: Two new concepts for Gringo went live on Friday, flirtedtoohard and lipsync, plus dreamlife for Thailand. After three days, Philippines iOS and Spanish iOS worked, both up to about 0.53. Philippines Android got worse with the same ads. In Thailand dreamlife is already #1; ROAS came down from 0.72 but stays above 0.40, so we watch it. English barely took the new ads, and iOS English fell to 0.38.

actions.title: Gringo EN needs a new concept; the rest stays on

rows.action: New concept, one set for both OS: flirtedtoohard got 0.5–1.4%. iOS EN fell 0.54 → 0.38 on combo (#1 for 6 weeks).
Refresh again: lipsync is #3 at 10%, ROAS 0.25 → 0.28.
Keep flirtedtoohard, lipsync and dreamlife on: worked in iOS ES and PH (0.53–0.55); watch TH (0.72 → 0.46).
Pause the batch ads: 32% of spend while ROAS fell 0.42 → 0.36 (iOS PH went up with the same ads).
Last week’s pause isn’t done: the creator couple ads are still #1 (56%), about $90 a day.
Gringo EN · Android (0.40) and PT (0.60): airport carries them.

actions.foot: Read on 3 days (6–8 Nov). Priority numbers run across the deck.
actions.note: Gringo had the most wins this week, in Spanish and Philippines iOS, so those ads stay on. English is the gap: the new ads didn't get spend and iOS English dropped, so English gets a new concept. Two media-buyer items, one of them still open from last week.

personas.title: Mature Dating Refresh: Banner
personas.sub: Result: 2 almost, 1 flat, 1 got worse · wanted still holds 94% of iOS EN
personas.foot: Before = 28 Oct – 3 Nov · After = 4–8 Nov (5 days) · all four are Mature 30to40 adsets
personas.note: Mature got 18 banner files on Wednesday, in English, Japanese and Korean. Wanted still owns iOS English with 94 percent, so banner can't move it. Android is flat at 0.30. Japan and Korea are far under the bar with or without banner: 0.19 and 0.07.

actions.title: Mature EN: refresh wanted, and stay close to Linda

rows.action: New visual · a Linda twin: a woman in her 30s, beach selfie, name, age and city, “serious relationship only”.
0.21 and 0.11, wanted #1 for 13 weeks: more creative, or less budget?
Cut or pause: 0.11; banner took #1 and ROAS fell further.

actions.foot: Linda (“Linda from Barcelona, 33, serious relationship only”) has led iOS since June at 94%. The 8 new wanted faces in August (Mei, Emma, James…) peaked at 4–34%.
actions.note: Yes, we refresh wanted, but history says how. Since June one ad, Linda from Barcelona, has carried 94 percent of iOS. In August we tried eight new faces, older women and men from other countries, and none beat her. So the new visual stays close to Linda: a woman in her thirties, a beach selfie, the same serious-relationship line.

personas.title: Sexy Female Lover Refresh: Wanted
personas.sub: Result: 1 worked · ROAS up to 0.73 in 3 days
personas.foot: Before = 30 Oct – 5 Nov · After = 6–8 Nov (3 days) · 4 of the files carry a Batch 42 label · Leave: keep the wanted variants on, re-read next week
personas.note: One adset, one result: new wanted variants took 38 percent in three days and ROAS jumped from 0.19 to 0.73. Three days is early, so we leave it and re-read next week.

divider.title: Last week’s refresh, one week on
divider.text: Batch 40 went live 28–31 Oct. Here is its read last Tuesday next to its read now, with 8 to 11 days of data.
divider.note: Before the creator content, a quick look back at last week's refresh, now that it has more data.

followup.eyebrow: Batch 40 · read on 1 Nov vs 8 Nov
followup.title: Batch 40 one week on: one more worked, most of it faded
points: Friends iOS EN moved from almost to worked: 0.44, with internationalfriends at 15%.
Gringo PH: dreamlife is still #1 (32%) at 0.40, so it stays on watch.
Everywhere else the Batch 40 ads fell to 0–14% of spend: Gringo and Local Dating moved on without them.
followup.foot: Now = from upload to 8 Nov, so it includes the days after Batch 41 landed in the same adsets. Friends PT is paused.
followup.note: One week later, Batch 40 has one more worked, Friends iOS English, and dreamlife still leads Gringo Philippines. The rest faded: the ads lost their share and old winners took the adsets back. That is why most of this week's actions are new concepts, not more variants.

divider.title: Creator Creative as Ads
divider.text: No new creator batch this week. The 16 creator ads from Batch 44 (live Fri 30 Oct), read again after 10 days.
divider.note: No new creator content went live this week, so this section re-reads last week's creator ads with ten days of data.

creator.eyebrow: Live: Fri 30 Oct · 10 days of data
creator.sub: Top 3 in 6 of 12 adsets · #1 in Gringo ID and Loc. Dating Android ES · 1 worked, 2 got worse, 1 to watch
creator.foot: Before = 23–29 Oct · After = 30 Oct – 8 Nov · rows: creator in top 3 first (best → worst), then the rest (worst → best)
creator.note: Ten days in, creator ads are in the top 3 of six adsets and lead two of them. Only one is a clear win: Gringo Spanish Android, up from 0.22 to 0.46. Local Dating Spanish got worse on both OS, and in Gringo Indonesia the couple ads still lead at 0.26. Our own past winners still hold everything else.

actions.title: Pause the couple ads in Gringo ID and talkinghead in Loc. Dating ES

rows.action: The one creator win: #2 at 33%, ROAS 0.22 → 0.46. Keep it on and decode it for the next Gringo ES brief.
Pause the creator couple ads: #1 at 61% since 30 Oct, ROAS 0.25 → 0.26. Asked last week.
Pause the creator talkinghead: #2 at 26% while ROAS fell 0.44 → 0.39.
The new adset is led by the creator talkinghead (36%) at 0.21: re-read next week.
Gringo EN · Android: creator ad #3 at 12%, ROAS 0.50 → 0.45, still above 0.40: watch.

actions.foot: Read on 10 days (30 Oct – 8 Nov). The other six creator ads stayed outside the top 3: no action.
actions.note: One creator ad earned its place, in Gringo Spanish Android, so we keep it and learn from it. Two need pausing, and one of those was already on last week's list.

news.eyebrow: Account news · week 2 Nov vs 26 Oct
news.title: 7 new #1s; manyplaces lifts Mature iOS EN to 0.53
news.foot: Sorted by ROAS after, then by biggest improvement · Before = week of 26 Oct · After = week of 2 Nov
news.note: Seven adsets got a new top spender. The best news is Mature iOS English, where manyplaces took 65 percent and ROAS doubled to 0.53. Slavic iOS English moved up on combo. Christian iOS English went the other way: a new #1 and ROAS down to 0.39.

news2.eyebrow: Account news · week 2 Nov vs 26 Oct
news2.title: 9 creatives jumped into the top 3; Slavic PT and ES fell hard
news2.foot: Sorted by ROAS after, then by biggest improvement · Before = week of 26 Oct · After = week of 2 Nov
news2.note: Nine creatives jumped into a top 3. Pickyourasian helped Asian Lover Android up to 0.42. On the other end, Slavic Portuguese and Spanish both dropped hard as combo and slider moved in, and Sexy Male fell to 0.13.

actions.title: Learn from manyplaces and combo; check the Slavic and Sexy Male drops

rows.action: Decode manyplaces: new #1 at 65%, ROAS 0.25 → 0.53. A candidate for the Mature EN brief.
Combo took #1 (36%), ROAS 0.42 → 0.52.
Both fell hard (0.58 → 0.30, 0.35 → 0.21) as combo and slider moved in: check them before more spend.
0.29 → 0.13 with wanted at 70%: cut budget.
New #1 beatsyncedtext and ROAS 0.52 → 0.39: no budget change until next week.

actions.foot: New #1s are 1 week old: no budget increases on them yet.
actions.note: Two creatives to learn from, manyplaces and combo. Three adsets for the media buyer to check, where ROAS dropped hard.
